name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Monday 6 October 1986

clue.text: Composer returned script with a neat correction

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the abbreviation is read from right to left
a correction puts things into a different order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten script
the five letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer sends back a score with a tidy correction pencilled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Script' is not a writing style but a manuscript, so it shrinks to its usual two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was the Czech composer of Ma Vlast and The Bartered Bride.

indicators.note: to include is to take inside, so the unknown goes within the people word

blocks.note: people as men, man and man
x is the usual unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A population taking in a stranger from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes into the middle of MAN MAN. The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea; its people are Manx.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman is a native of the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.

indicators.note: made in reads as put inside, so the fool sits within the other letters

blocks.note: the end of the word 'into', taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool is turned into a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' is split in two: the fool goes IN the letters TO, giving T-ASS-O.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance poet who wrote Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Overlook GCE blunder - ten pound error

indicators.note: a blunder is a mistake, so the letters are muddled
an error gets things wrong, signalling that the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Ignore a slip in a school exam result, a ten-pound mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: GCE was the British school examination, the General Certificate of Education.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to attend to it, to overlook it.

blocks.note: first meaning: a device carrying an electric charge that gives jolts
second meaning: a lurid, melodramatic story

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like a price being asked, but it is electrical charge: a SHOCKER gives shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A shocker is informal for a lurid thriller or melodramatic novel meant to startle its readers.

blocks.note: first meaning: a short sword once hung from the belt
second meaning: the sword of Damocles was suspended by a hair, so it is a thing that hangs

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it read as the famous sword itself; the question mark asks what that sword famously did.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger was a short sword hung from a belt; the sword of Damocles hung over his head.

clue.text: In short, the best man has taken Egan out for a drink

indicators.note: in short means abbreviated, so the word for the best is shortened
taken out of its normal order, the name is scrambled

blocks.note: the champion, cut short
the letters of this name rearranged

explanation.surface: The best man takes Egan out for a drink at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' suggests a wedding, which suits the drink, but it means the champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Essayist has written letter on Norse settlements

indicators.note: settling things rearranges them, so the letters are placed in a new order

blocks.note: em is the name of the letter M
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: An essayist has written a letter about Viking colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norse settlements' suggests Viking colonies; 'settlements' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American writer famous for essays such as Self-Reliance.

clue.text: Very little indeed, as one in ten would appear

definitions.text: as one in ten would appear

blocks.note: first meaning: almost none at all

blocks.clueFragment: as one in ten would appear
blocks.note: second meaning: in the numeral 10, the 1 stands beside the 0, a zero

explanation.walkthrough: 'One in ten' sounds like a proportion, but it is the digit 1 in the written number 10, which sits beside a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means almost nothing; and in 10 the digit one literally stands beside zero, or nothing.

blocks.note: the plain meaning: the furthest points, the tips of something
the setter's hint: the frugal manage to make these meet, as the idiom has it

explanation.surface: A puzzle about extremes and thrift.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'make ends meet' means to live within a tight budget, which is where frugality comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are the extreme points or limits of anything, the farthest parts from the middle.

clue.text: Fresh eggs a change from fruit?

indicators.note: a change of order means these letters are rearranged into something new

blocks.note: green means new or unripe, fresh
the letters of this word together with the following A, rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh eggs would make a nice change from eating fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of 'a change' belongs to the anagram fodder and the word 'change' tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Greengages are a variety of small green plum, a fruit.

clue.text: One with bad poems to palm off

indicators.note: bad poems are badly made, so the letters of the word are put into a different order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor poet tries to fob off weak verses on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose something on a person is to foist or fob it off on them unfairly.

clue.text: Spring locks on the out side, as intruder might do

indicators.note: being on the outside means the hair word wraps around the water word

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar springs the locks from outside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring locks' looks like a verb and its object, but each word supplies a piece; the water goes in after the third letter of the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to enter another's property without permission, which is what an intruder does.

blocks.note: someone camping is in a tent
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A query about what a camping fee is for.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or plan, the purpose behind an action.

blocks.note: first meaning: convenient or advantageous, adjective
second meaning: a device or means to an end, noun

explanation.walkthrough: The same word serves as adjective and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient as an adjective means advantageous or fitting; as a noun it is a convenient means to an end.

indicators.note: manufacturing makes something new out of raw material, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An element in the making of silver netting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factor' looks like a cause, but here it is the older sense of an agent acting for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a person who acts on behalf of another, especially in buying and selling; an agent.

clue.text: Point to work in church as field of activity

indicators.note: in places the work abbreviation within the church abbreviation

blocks.note: S for south, a point of the compass
CE is the Church of England
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone points to work in a church as their area of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a verb, but a compass point gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope is the range or extent of an activity or subject, the area it covers.

blocks.note: first meaning: a trailing or climbing plant such as ivy
second meaning: something that inches along, as a slow, stealthy mover does

explanation.walkthrough: Read whole it sounds like a slow-growing shrub; the second half describes a thing that moves at a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A creeper is a plant that spreads along the ground or up walls, and also one who creeps slowly.

clue.text: Sculptor joins old Noel at resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting these letters in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these three words rearranged

explanation.surface: A sculptor meets the aged Noel at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a seaside town, but it is the anagram signal: re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was the Florentine Renaissance sculptor famous for his bronze David.

blocks.note: first meaning: very old, of long ago
second meaning: an archaic word for an ensign, the officer who held up the flag

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept up standards' sounds like moral rigour; standards are flags. In Shakespeare, Iago is Othello's 'ancient', his ensign.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old; as an archaic noun it is a standard-bearer, an ensign carrying the flag.

clue.text: Girl writes nothing about a complaint - upsetting

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the zero word goes round the other pieces
upsetting tips something over, so in a down clue the letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: nil means nothing
taken as written
an ill is an ailment, a complaint

explanation.surface: A girl writes in about an upsetting grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: The ailment goes inside the zero word just after its first letter, and the whole is read upwards. 'Writes' does no work in the wordplay and only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lillian is a girl's given name.

indicators.note: something needing correction is wrong as it stands, so the letters are put right in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five high-speed rates have to be adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective describing the rates, but it is the verb meaning to go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food; to starve is to suffer or die from lack of food.

clue.text: Retrench about daily opening in Worcestershire town

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the word is used
about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the single letter

blocks.note: read as RE plus trench, and a trench is a ditch
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Cutbacks around the opening of a daily paper in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrench' looks like a single word for cutting back, but it splits as RE plus trench. Worcestershire is a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Redditch is a town in north-east Worcestershire, England, historically known for needle making.

clue.text: Labour politician seen on Red Square?

blocks.note: first meaning: Barbara, a leading minister in the Wilson governments
second meaning: the fortress of the Kremlin stands beside this Moscow square

explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Castle was a prominent British Labour cabinet minister. 'Red' nods to Labour's left, but the Square is Moscow's, where the Kremlin fortress stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Castle was a Labour minister; the Kremlin is a walled fortress, a castle, on Red Square.

blocks.note: first meaning: having a fine edge, acute
second meaning: a note a musician plays, raised a semitone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen to play' reads as eager for a game; the second half points to music, where a sharp is a note to be played.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp means keen-edged or acute; a sharp is also a musical note raised by a semitone.

clue.text: Look for the sort of canape that contains fruit

indicators.note: contains means the fruit word is held within the snack word
a sort of something is a variant of it, so the combined letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Seeking a kind of canape with fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the rearrangement works on all ten letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: Appearance is the way something looks, its outward aspect.

indicators.note: half keeps only four of the eight letters, a run taken from inside the word

blocks.note: four letters running from the second, half the word's length

explanation.surface: A writer who is half starved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' here is a run of half the letters from inside the word, not its front or back half.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis, and his son Martin, are well-known English novelists.

blocks.note: first meaning: squander, usually with 'away'
second meaning: a piece of battered and fried food

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests leftovers; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away is to waste; a fritter is a fried piece of fruit or meat in batter.

blocks.note: the surface reading: pay enough to live on
the setter's reading: a living is a church benefice, so this is a clergyman's pay

explanation.walkthrough: A 'living' is the post and income of a parish priest; the clergy's salary has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, especially the salary of a member of the clergy.
